etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English melten, from a merger of Old English meltan (intransitive) and mieltan (transitive), both meaning “to melt, digest,” from Proto-West Germanic *meltan and *maltijan, from Proto-Germanic *meltaną and *maltijaną, both from Proto-Indo-European *(s)meld- (“melt”). Cognate with Icelandic melta (“to digest”).

definitions.definition: (ergative) To change (or to be changed) from a solid state to a liquid state, usually by a gradual heat.

quote.citation: 2008 October, Davy Rothbart, “How I caught up with dad”, in Men's Health, volume 23, number 8, →ISSN, page 110:
quote.text: I gave him a couple of Advil and, after a few minutes, urged him back onto the track. Over the next few laps his pained expression slowly melted, although he still shuffled with a slight limp.

definitions.definition: (transitive, figurative) To soften, as by a warming or kindly influence; to relax; to render gentle or susceptible to mild influences; sometimes, in a bad sense, to take away the firmness of; to weaken.

quote.citation: c. 1605–1608, William Shakespeare, “The Life of Tymon of Athens”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene iii]:
quote.text: Thou would'st have  […]  melted down thy youth.

quote.citation: 1687, John Dryden, A Song for Cecilia's Day:
quote.text: For pity melts the mind to love.

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Canto XXI, page 35:
quote.text: The traveller hears me now and then,⁠And sometimes harshly will he speak:⁠‘This fellow would make weakness weak,And melt the waxen hearts of men.’

definitions.definition: (intransitive, figurative) To be emotionally softened or touched.
(intransitive, colloquial) To be very hot and sweat profusely.
Molten material, the product of melting.

quote.citation: 2012, Chinle Miller, In Mesozoic Lands: The Mesozoic Geology of Arches and Canyonlands National Parks, Kindle edition:
quote.text: The crust (a mere 1% of the Earth's volume) is made of lighter melt products from the mantle.

definitions.definition: The transition of matter from a solid state to a liquid state.
The springtime snow runoff in mountain regions.

quote.citation: 2002, Tod Dimmick, Complete idiot's guide to 20-minute meals:
quote.text: I recently asked a group of people whether they had eaten tuna melts as a kid. Everyone remembered a version of this dish.

definitions.definition: (geology) Rock showing evidence of having been remelted after it originally solidified.
A wax-based substance for use in an oil burner as an alternative to mixing oils and water.
